original_question: Sketch-and-solve: Let (A R^n x d ) be a full-rank matrix, (B R^n x p ) be a matrix, and let (Omega R^n x k ) be an oblivious subspace injection with dimension $d$ and injectivity (1-epsilon ). Let (~ X = (Omega^ -> p A)^+(Omega^ -> p B) R^d x p ) be the sketch-and-solve approximation to the ordinary least-squares solution $X = A^+B$. (Here, $^+$ denotes the Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse.) Prove or disprove: Does it necessarily hold that [ |A ~ X - B |_ F <= (1+O(epsilon)) _X R^d x p |AX - B |_ F? ]
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies the sketch-and-solve least-squares setting, the matrix shapes A in R^{n x d}, B in R^{n x p}, the use of an oblivious subspace injection with dimension d and injectivity 1-epsilon, the estimator X~ = (Omega^T A)^+ (Omega^T B), the ordinary least-squares solution X = A^+ B, and the precise relative-error question in Frobenius norm. In substance, it is essentially Problem 5.1.
missing_details: The paper works over the real numbers R; the field is not left open.
For A in R^{n x d}, 'full-rank' means full column rank, i.e. rank(A)=d (so n >= d).

To be stand-alone, the term 'oblivious subspace injection' must be unpacked using Definition 5.1: isotropy E||Omega^T x||_2^2 = ||x||_2^2 for all x in R^n, plus injectivity on every fixed d-dimensional subspace V.
Because Omega is random, the OSI definition includes a failure probability delta; when delta is omitted, the paper treats it as some fixed small constant (for example delta = 0.01).
The transpose should be written explicitly as Omega^T; the paper is in the real setting, so no adjoint/conjugate-transpose ambiguity is intended.
The right-hand side is explicitly min_{X in R^{d x p}} ||AX-B||_F; although this equals ||A(A^+B)-B||_F because A has full column rank, the optimization form is part of the official statement.

The probabilistic mode of the conclusion is implicit in the paper’s shorthand wording; for a fully stand-alone question one should say that the claimed guarantee is to hold with the success probability associated with the OSI event.
The paper presents this as an open 'prove or disprove' problem, not as a claim already known to be true.
refined_question: Let A in R^{n x d} have full column rank, let B in R^{n x p}, and let Omega in R^{n x k} be a random matrix that is an oblivious subspace injection for d-dimensional subspaces with injectivity 1-epsilon, in the sense that E||Omega^T x||_2^2 = ||x||_2^2 for every x in R^n, and for every fixed d-dimensional subspace V subseteq R^n one has (1-epsilon)||x||_2^2 <= ||Omega^T x||_2^2 for all x in V with probability at least 1-delta, where delta is some fixed small constant (suppressed in the paper when unspecified). Define the sketch-and-solve estimator X~ := (Omega^T A)^+ (Omega^T B) in R^{d x p}, and let X := A^+ B, equivalently the unique minimizer of min_{Y in R^{d x p}} ||AY-B||_F. Prove or disprove: does the OSI assumption alone force the relative-error bound ||AX~ - B||_F <= (1 + O(epsilon)) min_{Y in R^{d x p}} ||AY - B||_F (with the corresponding success probability over Omega)?
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 5.1 almost verbatim. The surrounding Section 5.1 discussion first defines OSE/OSI precisely in Definition 5.1, then frames a meta-problem asking for the weakest sketching assumption needed by a given algorithm, and then states Problem 5.1 exactly for sketch-and-solve least squares. The nearby context also explains why this problem is being asked: OSIs are already known to give constant-factor accuracy, and the open question is whether a higher-quality OSI (injectivity 1-epsilon) is enough for a (1+O(epsilon)) relative-error guarantee. The adjacent Problem 5.2 is only an analogue for randomized SVD, not an equivalent reformulation of Problem 5.1, so no alternate equivalent formulation should be added.
